elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New §21.3: "each Party's aggregate liability to each other Party arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the limit runs to and against every Party equally, and no retained language states that our liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: §21.3 caps at "the fees and charges paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" with no greater-of construction and no USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion-of-damages sentence exists anywhere in §4.9, §21.1–21.3 or §31; the rendered text contains no reference to indirect, consequential, special or incidental damages.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 opening exception: "Except in respect of ... its breach of its confidentiality obligations under Paragraph 31 ... none of which is subject to the limit set out in this Subparagraph 21.3"; Paragraph 31 is the retained CONFIDENTIALITY clause, so the cross-reference resolves.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The §21.3 carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; data protection and security obligations are not carved out.
§21.3: "Except in respect of a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2 ... none of which is subject to the limit"; §21.2 is the retained mutual third-party indemnity.
§21.3 excepts "its gross negligence" from the new limit.
§21.3 excepts "its wilful misconduct" from the new limit.
Fraud does not appear in the §21.3 carve-out list or elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in §21.3; the exception list stops at wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: §21.3 contains no statement that a Party's payment obligations (contributions, fees and charges) are not "damages" subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.3 binds "each Party's aggregate liability to each other Party" — symmetrical, with no one-sided protection retained (§4.9 remains a PG-specific performance disclaimer, not a cap).

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "shall not exceed the fees and charges paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis using the favourable "paid or payable" formulation.
§21.3 expressly places "a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2" outside the new limit.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 places "breach of its confidentiality obligations under Paragraph 31" outside the new limit; Paragraph 31 exists and is headed CONFIDENTIALITY, so the reference is not dangling.
"its gross negligence" is listed in the §21.3 exception.
"its wilful misconduct" is listed in the §21.3 exception.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: mutual cap, 12-month fee basis with "paid or payable", and carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all appear in operative language in new Subparagraph 21.3, not merely in the comment.

Preferred level fails on six elements: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud, infringement of the other Party's IP, or a statement that payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. These are correctly characterised as shortfalls from preferred, not separate deviations.

Minimality holds: a single inserted subparagraph for a clause that did not exist, no deletions, no edits to §4.9, §21.1, §21.2 or §31, and no extras such as survival tails, notice procedures or added damages categories. The closing sentence preserving the Schedule B share limitation is not gratuitous boilerplate — because indemnification is carved out of the new cap, that sentence is needed to stop the carve-out being read as displacing the Customer-favourable per-Party share limit in §21.2.

Intent is preserved: several-not-joint liability (§21.1), the mutual third-party indemnity and its Schedule B contribution ceiling (§21.2), the PG performance disclaimer (§4.9) and the confidentiality regime (§31) all survive without contradiction, and both internal cross-references (21.2 and 31) resolve.

Actionable point for the drafter, not a failure of the fallback: "fees and charges paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement" is undefined in this cost-sharing consortium document, where Parties fund construction via Schedule B shares rather than paying fees to one another. If the counterparty accepts, confirm in negotiation that the basis captures Schedule B contributions and other amounts payable (or add the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor from the preferred position) so the cap is not illusory in either direction.
If pressing toward preferred, the single highest-value additions are a mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion and carve-outs for data protection/security breaches and fraud.
